keyChanges.title: Samsung Completes AI5 Foundry Tape-Out for Taylor 2nm; Mass Production Still 2027
keyChanges.description: A Samsung Foundry principal engineer (James Kim) disclosed on LinkedIn that the Tesla-Samsung AI5 chip has reached foundry tape-out and is scheduled for manufacturing at Samsung's Taylor, Texas fab on Samsung's 2nm process. Yonhap, ET News, TrendForce, Tom's Hardware, and Electrek all covered the disclosure (the LinkedIn post was later deleted). This is a foundry-side tape-out — distinct from Tesla's April 2026 design tape-out that Musk announced — and is the first concrete Samsung production timeline public detail for AI5. Key new details: (1) AI5 will run on 2nm at Taylor, not a more mature node as previously assumed (2nm was expected for AI6); (2) AI5 volume is split between Samsung and TSMC, with TSMC's AI5 version having taped out months earlier; (3) Samsung will fully handle AI6 while TSMC handles AI6.5; (4) Taylor targets initial operations late 2026 and volume production in H2 2027. Critical reality check: tape-out is not production. Musk has said Tesla needs several hundred thousand completed AI5 boards before vehicle line switchover — still expected mid-to-late 2027. AI5 remains nearly two years behind original timelines, Cybercab launches on AI4, and Samsung Foundry continues operating at a loss (~KRW 600B estimated in non-memory for Q2).

positive_signals: Samsung foundry-side AI5 tape-out completed — design locked for Taylor 2nm manufacturing
AI5 confirmed dual-sourced: Samsung (Taylor 2nm) + TSMC (version taped out months earlier)
Putting AI5 on 2nm (not just AI6) signals Samsung 2nm yield may have crossed viability threshold (~60% assumed)
Taylor fab equipment move-in since April 2026; initial ops targeted late 2026, volume H2 2027
AI6 exclusive to Samsung under $16.5B deal; AI6.5 assigned to TSMC — clearer supply allocation
Korean engineering samples (KR 2613 marking) already demonstrated by Musk in May 2026
negative_signals: Tape-out is NOT production — engineering samples and qualification still required before mass production
High-volume AI5 still mid-to-late 2027; vehicles won't get meaningful AI5 until 2028 at earliest
AI5 nearly 2 years behind original schedule; Cybercab still launching on outdated AI4 hardware
TSMC AI5 version taped out months ahead of Samsung — Samsung remains the lagging foundry partner
Samsung Foundry still loss-making (~KRW 600B non-memory operating loss estimated Q2 2026); recovery depends on unproven 2nm yields at Taylor
No confirmed yield data published; 2nm process risk remains the gating item for both AI5 volume and AI6 (already slipped to mid-2028)
LinkedIn disclosure was unofficial and deleted — not a formal Samsung or Tesla production announcement

keyChanges.title: Giga Berlin 4680 production video drops — early ramp PR, full scale still H1 2027
keyChanges.description: On July 16, 2026, BASENOR reported Tesla released a short video of the 4680 cell line at Gigafactory Berlin (circulated via Sawyer Merritt on X the same day). The piece frames production as having begun May 12, 2026 — under ten weeks before the video — with full-scale expanded output still targeted only for H1 2027. Capacity narrative is unchanged: +$250M to raise the Berlin annual target from 8 GWh to 18 GWh (~$1.45B cumulative battery investment at the site). Dry Battery Electrode (DBE) for anode and cathode is restated as the manufacturing story, not a new process milestone. BASENOR also cites autoevolution that 'Made in Germany' Model Ys with locally produced 4680 cells are expected late Q3 2026 — a consumer timeline that remains single-source and unverified by Teslarati/TeslaNorth/Tesla IR this week. Applications for the JUNI x Tesla Battery Cell Giga Challenge (launched July 6) remain open through July 24, underscoring that manufacturing bottlenecks are still being crowdsourced. No new yield %, actual GWh output, or cost-per-kWh figures were published with the video.

keyChanges.title: Tesla registers 58 more Model Y robotaxis in Texas — fleet to 175 in one day
keyChanges.description: On July 15, 2026, Tesla Robotaxi LLC added 58 Model Y vehicles to Texas's automated-vehicle registry in a single day, lifting the company's Texas-registered robotaxi pool from 117 to 175 (~50% overnight). Texas Autonomous Vehicle Tracker, TeslaNorth, Basenor, and EVXL all corroborate the DMV-based jump — the largest one-day registration step visible on the public tracker. Dallas Tesla Club cross-checked VINs against the state registry. Competitive context: Waymo still leads Texas registrations at 642, Avride at 317, Tesla at 175, Zoox at 44. Critical caveat: registration is inventory/authorization pipeline, not proven rider-serving capacity. Service still runs on Model Y, not production Cybercab; software/safety constraints — not car availability — remain the binding limit. Hot-context active commercial fleet was ~20 vehicles across cities; a registration surge does not by itself reverse year-long scaling failure if unsupervised utilization stays thin.

Texas registered pool now 175 vehicles (up from 117 on July 14)
Multi-source corroboration: Texas AV Tracker, TeslaNorth, Basenor, EVXL; Dallas Tesla Club VIN check
Shows Tesla still batching fleet intake rather than freezing expansion
negative_signals: Registration ≠ active rider-serving fleet; prior active commercial fleet still ~20 vehicles after ~1 year
All 58 additions are Model Y — purpose-built Cybercab still not in commercial robotaxi service
Tesla remains 3rd in Texas AV registrations: Waymo 642, Avride 317, Tesla 175, Zoox 44
Software/safety constraint on unsupervised FSD still the bottleneck, not vehicle count

key_metrics.trajectory: Registration pipeline accelerating in batches; commercial utilization and Cybercab deployment still lag

keyChanges.title: Tesla claims wheelchair-accessible robotaxi 'active product' in Texas — no timeline
keyChanges.description: On July 13, 2026, Tesla Senior Policy Advisor India Herdman told the Washington D.C. City Council that Tesla is 'in development for a purpose-built, wheelchair-accessible autonomous vehicle' being built in Texas, citing paratransit difficulty and permanent wheelchair users' need for free movement. Covered by Wired, Teslarati, and Electrek. No model name, specs, or launch date given. Current commercial robotaxi fleet is Model Y (not wheelchair-accessible); production Cybercab is also not wheelchair-accessible (only braille controls and transfer-height seating). Herdman did not say whether this is the long-stalled Robovan or a new body style. Claim was made while lobbying on a DC bill that could allow robotaxi operations — not as an engineering milestone. Waymo also admitted at the same hearing it has no fully wheelchair-accessible driverless platform. ADA/DOJ pressure on ride-hail accessibility is rising (DOJ sued Uber in Sept 2025).

Consistent with Musk 'Absolutely' reply (Sept 2025) and Robotaxi app accessibility tab
negative_signals: Zero timeline, specs, chassis identity, or regulatory path disclosed

No US robotaxi operator offers fleetwide driverless WAV service — including market leader Waymo

key_metrics.actual: Policy statement only; 0 wheelchair-accessible vehicles in Tesla robotaxi fleet
key_metrics.trajectory: Claim without schedule; accessibility remains an unsolved product and regulatory gap

keyChanges.title: Miami robotaxi first rides expose tiny geofence, cancellations, and support interventions
keyChanges.description: More than a week after the July 3 Miami unsupervised launch (already covered in hot context), TeslaOracle published first-impression reporting on July 14 detailing operational friction. Geofence is only ~10–20 square miles (West Miami, parts of Doral/Sweetwater/Coral Gables). YouTubers from The Road to Autonomy and David Moss had rides cancelled twice (lightning + unknown), struggled to get a car due to small fleet vs demand, watched a Model Y arrive then leave without pickup, then sat in a vehicle that would not move until they called Tesla Support via the rear screen. A piece of tree bark on the road froze the car for 4 minutes 45 seconds with no rider disengage option. Positive notes: unsupervised operation with no safety rider, handled flooded streets/puddles, and some local users (e.g. Justin Berman) called the experience better than traditional ride-hail. Reality: geographic expansion without fleet depth produces poor availability and brittle edge-case handling — classic failed-scale pattern.

Handled mildly flooded Miami streets without apparent confusion

key_metrics.target: City-scale unsupervised robotaxi with reliable ETAs
key_metrics.trajectory: Geographic logo on the map without density or reliability of a real network

keyChanges.title: Texas permit lists Cleaning Robot at Austin Robotaxi hub (Ben White Blvd)
keyChanges.description: A July 13 Teslarati report on Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation filing TABS2025022006 for Tesla's Austin Robotaxi hub at 5900 E Ben White Blvd lists scope including a 'Cleaning Robot' plus Supercharger cabinets and an Equipment Inspection System. Aligns with Tesla's Jan 31, 2025 'This robot sucks' cabin-cleaning arm demo for Cybercab. Narrative is fully autonomous turnaround: drop passenger → return to hub → clean → charge → inspect → redispatch. Infrastructure signal is real but early — a permit line-item is not a working autonomous cleaning loop at scale. Does not expand commercial fleet or solve unsupervised driving constraints.

keyChanges.title: Italy confirms Tesla FSD application under review via Dutch homologation recognition
keyChanges.description: On or around July 13, 2026, Servedio Gaetano, General Director at Italy's Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport, confirmed on LinkedIn that Tesla 'only recently' submitted an application requesting recognition of the Dutch FSD homologation, and that the matter is 'in the analysis phase also based on the indications from the European community.' An Italian senator had previously urged prioritization after Netherlands approval. Critical read: this is an application receipt, not an approval. No timeline was given. Italy would be a major EU volume market if approved, but the fact that a large member state is still running a national analysis months after Dutch type approval undercuts Tesla's earlier claim that EU-wide mutual recognition would deliver broad summer-2026 access without repeating review. As of this week FSD Supervised remains live only in five EU countries: Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, and Belgium — none of which are top-tier European auto markets by volume.

Path is mutual recognition of Dutch homologation — faster than a full de novo type approval
Review explicitly references European Community guidance, consistent with EU mutual-recognition framework

keyChanges.title: FSD Supervised hits 50M km in Europe across five small markets; major markets still closed
keyChanges.description: Tesla announced that owners in the Netherlands, Estonia, Belgium, Lithuania, and Denmark have surpassed 50 million kilometres (~31 million miles) of FSD Supervised driving as of July 14, 2026 — roughly three months after the first EU approval (Netherlands, April 10). Uptake in approved markets is real and fast. Critical reality check: Europe's 50M km is ~0.26% of Tesla's ~12B global FSD miles, and the five live countries are small Baltic/Nordic/Benelux markets. Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and the UK — the volume markets that matter for Robotaxi economics and FSD attach rates — still have no consumer FSD Supervised. Belgium (approved ~June 10) is now confirmed as the fifth European country, updating the prior 'Denmark = fourth' count. Mutual recognition is expanding, but slowly and only into secondary markets so far.

Belgium activation completes fifth-country footprint via mutual recognition pathway

keyChanges.title: FSD fleet hits 12 billion cumulative supervised miles; training data grows, software still on v14
keyChanges.description: As of ~July 17, 2026 Tesla FSD (Supervised) fleet miles surpassed 12 billion globally, roughly one month after the 11 billion mark (June 9). Community tracking cited by TeslaNorth estimates 26–30 million new miles per day, with >4.5 billion of the total on city streets. Europe contributed 50M+ km across five small approved markets. Critical framing for the software roadmap: data volume continues to accelerate and feeds RL hard-example mining (explicitly referenced in v14.3.5 release notes for traffic lights, rare objects, animals). But cumulative miles are not a substitute for the delayed v15 10B-parameter architectural overhaul. Tesla has already stated current v14 is not safe enough for large-scale robotaxi expansion without 'major architectural improvements' — more supervised miles improve the current model but do not ship the next architecture. Metric is community-tracked, not an official Tesla IR disclosure.

Daily accumulation estimated at 26–30M miles/day — rapid data flywheel
>4.5B miles on city streets — hardest domain for end-to-end driving
v14.3.5 release notes explicitly credit fleet-sourced hard RL examples for traffic lights, rare objects, animals

keyChanges.title: NTSB preliminary report: driver overrode FSD at 100% accelerator in fatal Katy, TX crash
keyChanges.description: On July 15, 2026 the NTSB released preliminary findings on the June 19 fatal Model 3 crash in Katy, Texas. Electronic data confirmed FSD Supervised was engaged on a 30 mph residential street, the system had begun slowing for a stop, then the driver pressed the accelerator to 100%, reaching >70 mph (Tesla VP Ashok Elluswamy previously said 73 mph) before striking a home and killing 76-year-old Martha Avila. Security footage and phone searches ('Tesla FSD not aggressive enough 2026', 'Tesla FSD too timid') contradict the driver's claim he passed out. Driver Michael Butler faces manslaughter charges; the victim's family still sues both Butler and Tesla. Critical reality: this preliminary report supports Tesla's case that software did not command the fatal acceleration, but (1) NTSB investigation is ongoing with possible safety recommendations still ahead, (2) NHTSA opened its own Special Crash Investigation, (3) the broader NHTSA Engineering Analysis EA26002 covering 3.2M vehicles for FSD visibility/degradation failures remains open and unresolved, and (4) the event re-emphasizes that FSD is SAE Level 2 — drivers can and do override with catastrophic results. Not a regulatory win that clears the path to unsupervised FSD.

positive_signals: NTSB vehicle data independently confirms driver accelerator override to 100% — aligns with Tesla/Ashok account
FSD had begun slowing for stop before override — system behavior consistent with supervised L2 design
Driver charged with manslaughter; criminal focus is on human, not vehicle software in this incident
Multi-source corroboration (Teslarati, TeslaNorth, Drive Tesla Canada)
negative_signals: NTSB investigation still open — probable cause and safety recommendations not issued
NHTSA Special Crash Investigation also open on this crash
Broader NHTSA EA26002 (3.2M vehicles, visibility/glare/fog failures, pre-recall stage) still unresolved since March 2026
Civil lawsuit against Tesla continues despite driver-override finding
Phone searches show user frustration with FSD 'timidity' — product/UX risk that drivers will override aggressively
Reinforces that FSD Supervised remains fully driver-responsible Level 2 — no regulatory path to unsupervised cleared by this report

keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.5 rolls out: incremental RL polish, still no v15 path visible
keyChanges.description: On July 13, 2026 Tesla began rolling out software update 2026.20.6.6 with FSD (Supervised) v14.3.5 for HW4/AI4 vehicles (S/3/X/Y/Cybertruck). Official release notes claim: upgraded RL training stage, upgraded neural network vision encoder (rare/low-visibility, 3D geometry, traffic signs), AI compiler/runtime rewrite with MLIR claiming 20% faster reaction time, mitigated lane-biasing/tailgating, more decisive parking, better emergency-vehicle/school-bus/animal/traffic-light handling, improved temporary degradation recovery, and unified model between Actually Smart Summon, FSD, and Robotaxi. QoL features include Camera Preview while driving, FSD live indicator in the Tesla app, intervention-free distance tracking, and parking options on the map. Critical reality: this is another point-release on the v14.3.x branch — still fully Supervised (SAE L2), still requiring driver attention. TeslaFi stats at release showed only ~243 cars / ~1.9% of tracked fleet on 2026.20.6.6. Early impressions are mixed: NotATeslaApp/Zack reported fixed turn-lane twitch and better parking, while Teslarati and high-mileage tester David Moss reported 'horrible' parking (3 bad jobs in 23 min) and inconsistent speed profiles. Most importantly, there is zero public evidence of FSD v15 (the delayed 10B-parameter architectural overhaul) shipping, testing publicly, or advancing its end-2026/early-2027 target. Robotaxi scale remains explicitly blocked until v15 per Q1 2026 guidance. v14.3.5 is incremental supervised polish, not the unsupervised unlock.

keyChanges.title: Report: HW4 consumer FSD runs distilled Cybercab models — hardware tiering confirmed
keyChanges.description: On July 14, 2026 NotATeslaApp published an exclusive claiming Tesla develops FSD models first for Cybercab's more powerful FSD hardware, then distills them into smaller 'student' models for consumer HW4/AI4 vehicles — analogous to how FSD v14 Lite is a distilled v14 for HW3. The report argues this is good news for HW4 unsupervised hopes (HW4 still in the running, unlike HW3 which is permanently capped), because consumer cars receive optimized versions of the same robotaxi stack. Critical read: this is a single-source exclusive citing an unnamed source — confidence is low until corroborated. If true, it confirms a multi-tier capability hierarchy (Cybercab native > HW4 distilled > HW3 Lite ceiling) and implies consumer HW4 may never run the full-weight teacher model that Cybercab gets. Combined with the confirmed v15 delay and Cybercab-first development, it reinforces that unsupervised consumer FSD depends on distillation quality, not parity with robotaxi hardware. No official Tesla confirmation.

positive_signals: If accurate, HW4 remains on the unsupervised path (unlike HW3, which Tesla confirmed cannot do unsupervised FSD)
Cybercab-first development with distillation is a rational engineering path for multi-hardware fleets
Consistent with known v14 Lite distillation pattern for HW3
negative_signals: Single-source exclusive (NotATeslaApp) with unnamed source — no Tesla confirmation, no Teslarati/TeslaNorth corroboration
Implies consumer HW4 gets second-class/lighter models vs Cybercab native stack
Does not advance v15 ship date; distillation is process, not a capability milestone
Reinforces hardware tiering: Cybercab > HW4 distilled > HW3 Lite (permanent unsupervised exclusion for ~4M HW3 vehicles)
Vague on how much capability is lost in distillation — no metrics on student vs teacher performance gap

keyChanges.title: HW3 FSD v14 Lite completes claimed 4,255-mile zero-intervention coast-to-coast drive
keyChanges.description: On July 17, 2026 TeslaNorth reported that drivers Koby Pierce and 'Liam's Dad' completed a diagonal US coast-to-coast run (Key West, FL to Cape Flattery, WA — 4,255 miles) in a 2020 Model 3 Long Range (HW3, 175k+ miles) on FSD v14 Lite, claiming zero manual steering, braking, accelerator, or turn-signal inputs. The trip is part of a larger 'Buoy to Bay' expedition. Critical reality: this is a self-reported enthusiast demonstration, not an independent audit. Drivers remained in the vehicle (Supervised), so SAE L2 supervision was still present even if hands-off. HW3 remains officially capped at v14 Lite with no path to unsupervised FSD or v15 (confirmed Q1 2026). A successful supervised long-haul does not change the permanent hardware ceiling for ~4 million HW3 vehicles, nor does it substitute for the delayed v15 architectural upgrade needed for robotaxi scale. Treat as positive signal for v14 Lite highway reliability, not as unsupervised readiness.

High-mileage (175k+) 2020 Model 3 LR — stress test on older hardware and battery
Corroborates that v14 Lite can handle long-haul highway/intercity supervised driving on HW3

keyChanges.title: Shareholders put Optimus production ramp under Q2 earnings spotlight — no commercial path yet
keyChanges.description: Ahead of Tesla's July 22, 2026 Q2 earnings call, shareholder questions submitted via Say Technologies put Optimus Gen 3 at the center of investor scrutiny. The top question (by share-weighted votes) asks for the 'current status of Optimus Gen 3 production ramp,' tasks the robot will perform by end of 2027, and 'initial deployment in factories, and external sales timeline/volume for 2027.' Benzinga and Electrek both report Optimus among the most-upvoted topics. Electrek notes the soft production-status questions were whale-boosted (~4.8M shares each) while harder accountability questions on missed short-term goals dominate the rest of the top 20. Reality check: full-scale Fremont production is still only targeted for late July/August 2026; Musk already warned output will be 'extremely slow'; all 2026 units remain for internal testing with no commercial customers or pricing; and Tesla's $1T Musk pay package still hinges on 1M Optimus units among other milestones. Investors are asking for a production and sales roadmap Tesla has not delivered.

keyChanges.title: Agility Robotics opens Fremont training hub as Digit already earns revenue — Optimus still pre-commercial
keyChanges.description: On July 17, 2026, TechCrunch reported Agility Robotics is opening a 60,000-square-foot humanoid training facility in Fremont, California — just up the highway from Tesla's Fremont plant where Optimus full-scale production is expected this summer. Agility's Digit robot is already generating revenue moving totes/bins for Amazon, GXO, Schaeffler, and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, with ~$300M in contract orders. Agility is pursuing a reverse-merger expected to make it the first pure-play public humanoid company later in 2026. CEO Peggy Johnson emphasized Agility has already commercialized: safety/regulatory compliance, IT integration, and warehouse management system plug-in. Outside estimates put Digit deployments in the dozens (not thousands), but the competitive contrast is stark: Digit does paid warehouse work today while Tesla's deployed Optimus units still do no useful commercial work, and 2026 Optimus output is internal-only. Combined with Xpeng targeting 2027 global launch of its Iron robot (SCMP, July 16), the humanoid race is no longer Tesla-only narrative.

Tesla still has unmatched capital and manufacturing scale ambition (1M/yr Fremont, 10M/yr Giga Texas targets)

keyChanges.title: Elluswamy hails Optimus after S/X line teardown — confidence messaging, zero new production data
keyChanges.description: On or around July 13, 2026, Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy responded to Tesla Manufacturing's Model S/X decommissioning video (already covered July 10) with: 'Big shoes to fill, but I'm confident Optimus will not disappoint!!' Covered by Benzinga, Yahoo Finance, and others. VP of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy has said the facility could see up to ~40 production lines due to Optimus's complex design. This is leadership morale/PR on a facility conversion already in the tracker — not a production-start confirmation, yield figure, unit count, or capability demo. keyChanges.title: Tesla IR posts Q2 2026 earnings consensus: $27.6B revenue, 1.73M full-year deliveries, -$3.25B FCF
keyChanges.description: Ahead of the July 22 earnings call, Tesla published company-compiled Wall Street consensus from 23 sell-side firms (Barclays, BofA, Goldman, Morgan Stanley, etc.). Street expects Q2 total revenue of $27.58B (auto $20.05B, energy $3.77B, services $3.76B), adjusted non-GAAP EPS $0.55 / GAAP EPS $0.36, gross margin 19.5%, and operating margin only 5.4%. CapEx is pegged at $6.7B with expected free cash flow of -$3.25B for the quarter. Full-year vehicle delivery consensus sits at ~1.73M units — roughly 5–6% growth vs ~1.64M in 2025. That is modest given the Q2 delivery beat (480,126 vs ~406k consensus already reported July 2). H1 deliveries (~838k combining Q1 358,023 + Q2 480,126) imply Tesla needs ~892k H2 deliveries to hit the 1.73M full-year print. Negative FCF and sub-6% operating margin undercut the 'strong auto quarter' narrative: volume beat inventory, not a structural margin or cash-flow re-acceleration.

keyChanges.title: California $270M MyFirstEV rebate starts; Model 3/Y qualify but Tesla disadvantaged vs CA-based rivals
keyChanges.description: Gov. Newsom signed SB 168 creating a $270M point-of-sale EV rebate (MyFirstEV), split $135.5M state / $135.5M automaker-funded, to partially replace the expired $7,500 federal EV tax credit. First-time EV buyers get $3,500 off new BEVs with MSRP ≤$50,000; used EVs ≤$25,000 get $1,750. Tesla Model 3 RWD ($42,490), Model 3 LR ($47,490), and base Model Y ($44,990) all qualify. Model S/X/Cybertruck do not. Critical catch: California-based automakers (Rivian, Lucid) are carved out of the $50k price cap entirely — Tesla, headquartered in Texas since 2021, is not. Program goes live later this summer via CARB. Net: modest positive for base 3/Y CA demand, but structural disadvantage vs in-state competitors and only a partial patch for lost federal incentive in Tesla's largest US state market (~1/3 of US EV sales).

Vehicles for Latvia likely from Giga Berlin or Shanghai; Uruguay imports from Shanghai. Uruguay has high EV penetration (>20% BEV share) and near-100% renewable grid; Latvia BEV share ~7%. These are real market-entry milestones that expand the delivery footprint, but absolute volume contribution will be tiny vs Tesla's ~1.7M annual run-rate. Useful for long-tail growth and Shanghai export utilization, not a fix for modest full-year growth guidance.

keyChanges.title: Grimes County School Boards Approve $119B Terafab JETI Tax Deals 5-2 Amid Local Opposition
keyChanges.description: On July 14, 2026, Iola ISD and Anderson-Shiro CISD each voted 5-2 to approve all eight JETI school-property-tax agreements for TeraFab AI, LLC (SpaceX special-purpose entity) covering the proposed Terafab semiconductor complex near Gibbons Creek in Grimes County. Agreements grant a 10-year school M&O tax reduction per phase (freeze at ~50% of appraised value) in exchange for claims of up to $119B total investment across four phases, 4,234+ direct jobs, and ~22,000 acres. Phase 1 alone was previously filed at ~$10.37B; media also cite a ~$55B first-phase scale. SpaceX told districts that without the deals the project would likely relocate out of Texas (Arizona cited). Community opposition was strong over water use, noise/lighting, and loss of small-town character (Iola population ~300). School boards framed approvals as keeping the process alive, not final endorsement. Construction still needs Governor Abbott approval, three-party signing, and Comptroller filing—no permits or groundwater apps were on file as of mid-June reporting. SpaceX wants Phase 1 construction before year-end 2026.

keyChanges.title: Gov. Abbott Terafab JETI Decision Deadline Passes With No Public Yes/No; Deal Still Not Locked
keyChanges.description: Under Texas JETI rules, Governor Greg Abbott shared the same 30-day window as the school districts after Comptroller acceptance on June 15, 2026—closing July 15. After the July 14 school-board approvals, KBTX reported on July 16 that Abbott’s decision remained unknown past the deadline. Law allows up to seven additional days to formally notify parties, so an answer could slip into the following week. If Abbott votes no, the school approvals are void and the deal dies; SpaceX filings state the project could leave Texas without the agreements. If yes, parties must still formally sign and file with the Comptroller before Phase 1 construction can start. Separately on July 16, Grimes County commissioners tabled a local ‘accountability’ resolution meant to set clearer industrial-project standards (water, lighting, noise, transparency)—signaling unresolved community and governance friction even as tax deals advance.
